kit.name: ELEGOO UNO R3 Project Most Complete Starter Kit

identity.manufacturer: unbranded / generic (no manufacturer markings printed on the part)

generic_equivalents: Jameco Valuepro DC22 (22pF 50V Z5U ceramic disc)

function.one_sentence_plain_english: A tiny capacitor that stores a very small electric charge and is almost always used in a matched pair to help a quartz crystal start up and keep steady time.
function.what_it_is_used_for: This kit does not wire it into a single named lesson by itself. Its standard job, and the reason it is bundled at all, is as a load capacitor on the two legs of a quartz crystal on a microcontroller. The ATmega328 datasheet lists 12-22 pF as its recommended crystal load capacitor range, which is why kits built around the ATmega328 (the chip on the UNO) include 22pF capacitors.
function.how_it_works_briefly: Two conductive plates separated by a ceramic insulator. It charges and discharges almost instantly, far faster than an electrolytic capacitor, which is exactly the behavior a crystal oscillator circuit needs: two of these capacitors, one from each crystal leg to ground, present a combined load capacitance that lets the crystal oscillate at its rated frequency.

pinout.name: Lead A
pinout.notes: Either lead can connect to either side of the circuit; no polarity.

pinout.name: Lead B
pinout.notes: Electrically identical to Lead A and interchangeable with it.

pins.pin_1_identification: Not applicable. There is no positive lead. Both leads are electrically identical and can be swapped without changing the circuit.

electrical.operating_voltage: 0-50V DC (rated maximum, per a comparable retail part)
electrical.absolute_max_voltage: 50V DC (per Circuit Specialists 21CB022, a comparable 22pF 50V ceramic disc capacitor; ELEGOO's exact unit is not independently datasheet-confirmed)
electrical.typical_current: not applicable, passive component with no intrinsic current draw

key_specs.tolerance_percent: 5%, per Circuit Specialists 21CB022, a comparable retail part; ELEGOO's exact tolerance is not independently confirmed
key_specs.marking_code: Small values like 22pF are normally printed directly on the disc as '22', without the 3-digit EIA multiplier code used for larger values like '104'.
key_specs.typical_use_note: 12-22 pF is the crystal load capacitor range recommended by the ATmega328 datasheet, per discussion on the Arduino Forum.

visual_identification.shape_and_size: A small flat disc or rounded teardrop shape, roughly 5-6 mm across, with two straight wire leads coming out the bottom, spaced about 0.1-0.2 inch (2.5-5 mm) apart.
visual_identification.color_and_markings: Body color varies by supplier, commonly blue, yellow/tan, or brown. Printed with the number 22 (sometimes followed by a tolerance letter like J or K).
easily_confused_with: 104 ceramic capacitor: same disc shape and through-hole leads, but marked '104' instead of '22' and usually a visibly larger body since it holds much more capacitance
other small-value ceramic discs such as 33 or 47, distinguished only by the printed number

example_connections.uno_pin: one leg of an external quartz crystal (if used for its standard oscillator-load purpose), other end to GND
the crystal's other leg, other end to GND

required_extra_parts: a quartz crystal, if wired for its standard oscillator-load purpose (the UNO board itself already has its own crystal and load capacitors built in, so this loose part is for a separate breadboard oscillator circuit)

hazards: none under normal use within its 50V rating
exceeding the voltage rating can crack the ceramic or cause an internal short
handling_notes: handle by the body rather than repeatedly flexing the leads, which can fatigue and snap them
common_mistakes: confusing it with the visually similar 104 capacitor since both are small ceramic discs
using it where a much larger capacitance is needed; 22 pF is about 4,500 times smaller than the 104 capacitor's 100,000 pF (100 nF)

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: a breadboard crystal-oscillator circuit will not start, or a microcontroller runs at the wrong clock speed
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: load capacitance far from the crystal's rated value, a missing capacitor, or a bad connection
symptoms_and_causes.check: measure capacitance directly with a multimeter's capacitance mode and compare to 22 pF; confirm both leads are firmly connected

troubleshooting.how_to_test_with_a_multimeter: Set the multimeter to capacitance mode (the F or farad symbol) and clip the probes to the two leads; expect a reading close to 22 pF. Many basic multimeters only resolve down to nF or pF ranges with reduced accuracy at this small a value, so treat the reading as approximate.
